name: Beaver Tailwater
description: Seven miles of cold trout water on the White River, from Beaver Dam to Houseman Access. Dam releases and Table Rock Lake both shape it: the lake backs up to within about a mile of the dam, so some stretches paddle like a lake. Releases can raise the water fast, and a quiet dam doesn't mean easy water or a safe time to wade. Check posted signs and current Arkansas Game and Fish Commission trout rules before you go.
managingAuthority: USACE Little Rock District; Arkansas Game and Fish Commission

regulations.text: Beaver Tailwater: White River from 100 yards below Beaver Dam to the boat ramp at Houseman Access. No fishing, boating or wading within 100 yards of Beaver Dam.
regulations.authority: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission, regulation N1.03

openQuestions: Table Rock backwater: at Table Rock's conservation pool (915 ft) backwater reaches to within about a mile of Beaver Dam; the dam's own tailwater gauge read 916.35 ft on 2026-11-12. The reach stays unrated with float time withheld, and should show Table Rock's level as downstream context.
The three pending Table Rock lake launches (Beaver Lake Dam Site, Bertrand, Houseman) are these accesses: link or retire them once the access points exist.
